episode.title: Corrections, Trust, and the Long Game

bullets: A correction functions as a reliability signal rather than a failure — teams that ignore this pattern often end up rebuilding from scratch a year later.
Managing the risk of being wrong in public constitutes its own discipline, distinct from the underlying technical or editorial work.
The framing of reliability matters because it determines which tradeoffs are being made — the same decision looks different depending on the lens applied.
The pattern of treating corrections as signals has held consistently across three different teams, suggesting it is a general principle rather than a one-off observation.
Risk management crosscuts all other reliability concerns, making it the natural focal point for the most substantive part of the conversation.
A practical first step is to pick one of the discussed ideas and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration rather than wholesale transformation.
